chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Sindi ibn Al-Rabi', from Saeed ibn Janah, who said:
I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in his house in Medina, so he said initiating: 'The one who completes his Rukū, loneliness would not enter into him in the grave'.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of completing Rukū in prayer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the physical and spiritual completeness of Rukū to the psychological comfort of the soul in Barzakh, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the continuity of ritual precision into the afterlife. This teaching underscores how mindful devotion during prayer serves as a spiritual anchor, mitigating the existential isolation often described in Islamic eschatology. The hadith thus connects the microcosm of daily worship with the macrocosm of eternal destiny, affirming the transformative power of Salah.
